correctness.rationale: The coordinate-replication formula gives the exact identity \(\|T_\lambda x\|_p^p=\|\lambda\|_p^p\|x\|_p^p\), so each nonzero operator is injective and bounded below, hence has closed range. On every output block \(M_i\) the range is the one-dimensional pattern \(x_i\lambda\); choosing a coordinate vector outside \(\operatorname{span}\{\lambda\}\) gives infinitely many linearly independent quotient classes, so the algebraic codimension is infinite. If a finite-dimensional subspace had dense orbit, all positive iterates would vanish in the quotient and the quotient image of the orbit would be one finite-dimensional closed subspace, impossible in the infinite-dimensional Hausdorff quotient. This works for the quasi-Banach cases because only Hausdorff topological-vector-space facts are used.

originality.rationale: The advertised simultaneous finite-supercyclicity exclusion is already a direct consequence of published input. Bourdon--Feldman--Shapiro Lemma 1.1 states that every nontrivially finite-N-supercyclic operator has dense range. The focal 2026 construction is exactly the published coordinate-replication isometric copy used here; from that displayed construction alone its range is visibly nondense (indeed the output omits fixed coordinates and satisfies blockwise proportionality constraints). Thus every nonzero member of the published copy automatically fails every finite N-supercyclicity level. The strengthened infinite-codimension observation is an elementary blockwise reading of the same construction and does not rescue originality of the final theorem under the implication rule.
